# Launch checklist

A coordinated announcement touches every channel at once, which is exactly when
per-channel discipline is most likely to slip. The checklist exists so launch-day
adrenaline executes a plan instead of improvising one.

Before launch day: the canonical piece is final and evidence-checked; every channel
adaptation is drafted, claim-fidelity checked, and scheduled as drafts pending a
human send; the press brief is delivered to the spokesperson; the newsletter's place
in the cycle is decided rather than assumed; and every number in every artifact
traces to one shared evidence sheet, so a late correction propagates from a single
place.

On launch day: one named coordinator owns the send order and the go/no-go call per
channel; each send is confirmed against its checklist row as it happens; and
practitioner questions arriving in threads are answered by the discovery-qualified
standing process, not by whoever is nearest.

After launch: replies and corrections are tracked for a standing window; every
correction lands in the canonical piece first; and the retrospective records what
the checklist missed, amending it here the same week, because a checklist that does
not absorb its misses is ritual rather than protection.

An announcement that cannot complete the pre-launch rows on time moves its date. A
launch is coordinated evidence delivery, and the date serving the checklist — not
the reverse — is what keeps it honest under deadline pressure.
